units: sheet units: 1 unit = 100 sheet px (front + back true orthos; the side is a 3/4 view); floor z = 0 at the lowest mist wisp (it floats)

chain.rule: two strands of 8 closed stadium links per wrist hanging from the shackle ring (the sheet's two free-hanging strands); link planes alternate 90 deg (even links face the front)

grade.note: per-corner gradient: streak colours mix toward mist_lavender by 0.85 at z >= 3.0 -> 0 at z <= 1.8; alpha = region alpha (0.55) x (0.27 + 0.73 x ramp), ramp 1 at z >= 3.3 -> 0 at the floor: 0.55 under the tatters -> 0.15 at the bottom (gate 2026-10-11)

facing.rule: hood centre at eye height -> the midpoint of the two eyes (the face looks -Y)

mirror_test.rule: rest pose mirror-symmetric (house rule); the shell's residual = marching-tet triangulation + collapse decimation (fields and grid nodes are exactly symmetric)

tier_rationale: REGULAR role (a line unit): window [8000, 22000]. One smooth cloth / mist shell carries most of the budget (folds, hem tatters, mist bands need density under flat shading; the face zone is densified for the eye / slit outlines); 32 closed chain links + 2 shackles take the rest.

open_edges.rule: one closed SDF shell + closed tori (shackles) + closed stadium tubes (links)

sheet_deviations: SYMMETRY (house rule): the sheet's face + chest features sit 0.09 u to image right of the body axis (eye midpoint x 240.9 vs axis 232: the face drawn slightly turned) -> built centred on X = 0; the front mist's lower wisps drift to the unit's left (+X: front z 0.39 -0.55..1.31, back z 0.21 -1.50..0.51 mirrored) -> built symmetric

SIDE VIEW is a 3/4 drawing, not an ortho: every half-depth (head 0.82 x width, torso 0.40-0.47, skirt 0.70 x width), the sleeves' forward hang (wrist y -0.25) and the mist's backward trail (y-centre 0 -> +0.55 at the bottom) are estimates read off it

CHAINS: the brief says 'a hanging loop ... closed torus-link chain, 12-16 links per loop'; the SHEET draws, at each wrist, TWO strands hanging from the shackle with FREE ends (front x 52 / 85 px, bottoms y ~690-710) -> built as the sheet draws: 2 strands x 8 closed links = 16 per wrist (each link a closed tube; the strands do not join)

CHAIN COLOUR: the first link (at the shackle) and the free end link of each strand are dark iron (chain_iron, 38,39,43), the rest glow red, as drawn; the sheet's darker shading of the edge-on links is not painted
CHAIN PLANE: strands separate in X (front x -1.80 / -1.47) and hang straight; the sheet's slight curl / twist of the strands is not modelled

TATTERS: GEOMETRY -- the robe solid is clipped by a ring of 12 seeded pointed tatters (mirror-symmetric, tips z 2.50-3.00) hanging over an inset mist column; the tatters are solid wedges of the robe (no thin double-sided flaps), their cut undersides take the fold shadow

MIST: a closed rippled column + 20 strands of 7 closed blobs (fogeist approach), BLENDED alpha graded per corner down the height (no band steps), lavender-white with purple / pink-red streaks (streak regions are hard-edged region boundaries); the sheet's feathered smoke edges and fine curls are not modelled; the mist casts a solid shadow
EYES / SLITS: one flat glowing red region each, sunk 0.050 / 0.040 u; the sheet's brighter inner core, dark-red rim and soft halo are not modelled

FOLDS: soft vertical ridges + groove shadows on the robe below the chest and in the mist, plus underside shadow on the sleeves / drapes; the sheet's diagonal draping creases on the hood, shoulders and sleeves are not modelled
SLEEVE ENDS: the sheet shows no hands; each sleeve ends in a gathered rounded tuft just through the shackle
GLOW HALOS: the sheet's red glow aura round the chains / eyes is not geometry (emission only)
INK LINES: the thin dark contour lines are line art, not modelled

bake.cage_rule: 3 x the shell high->low sampled p99 distance (floor BAKE_CAGE_FLOOR 0.04)
bake.high_rule: the cloth SDF high (eyes + slits sunk) + every closed part
bake.normal_reference: FLAT low faces (the cloth reads smooth under the flat_shaded contract); wired into both materials

palette.provenance: pixel-sampled from the sheet's six palette chips + drawn-surface samples (see the palette notes)
